name: IP Geolocation Lookup
description: Geolocate a single IPv4 or IPv6 address. Returns country (name + ISO code), region (name + code), city, postal/ZIP, latitude/longitude (city-level precision, not GPS), timezone, ISP, organization, and AS number + name. Multi-gateway: the same lookup is available via four independent x402 providers at different prices and call conventions.

ip.description: IPv4 or IPv6 address to locate. Omit to geolocate the caller's IP.

usage.callShape: GET https://2s.io/api/geo/ip?ip={ipv4_or_ipv6} (default). Other gateways: auor.io GET ?ip=, x402node GET ?ip=, padelmaps POST JSON {ip}.
usage.outputShape: Default (2s.io) is double-nested: data.items[0].{ip,country.{code,name},region.{code,name},city,postalCode,coords.{lat,lon},timezone,network.{isp,org,asn}} + data.source + meta.cost.usd. NOTE: padelmaps & x402node return a FLAT object instead.
quirks: MULTI-GATEWAY, NOT uniform: only the default (2s.io) output is double-nested at data.items[0]; padelmaps and x402node return a FLAT object. Do not assume one parser works for all backends.

2s.io (default): use GET only. Sending POST returns 405 AFTER payment is deducted (non-refundable). Useful data is at body.data.items[0], country/region are OBJECTS ({code,name}), lat/lon are under coords, ISP/org/asn under network.
padelmaps backend genuinely requires POST with a JSON body {ip} (alias 'address'); omitting ip looks up the CALLER's IP. Costs $0.01 — 10x the default.
x402node backend is x402 version 1 (older protocol) and is an ipapi.co passthrough; $0.005.

auor.io is an IPStack passthrough; check_endpoint_schema throws 'Cannot read properties of null (reading ip-stack)' on the hyphenated path, but the endpoint works — verified via discover_api_endpoints.
Pricing varies 10x across gateways: 2s.io & auor.io $0.001, x402node $0.005, padelmaps $0.01. Prefer the default unless a specific output shape is needed.
Lat/lon is city-level, not GPS precision (per 2s.io schema).
2s.io supports bulk lookups (up to 100 IPs) via a different endpoint /api/ipinfo/bulk — out of scope for this single-IP service.
usage.guide: Geolocate a single IPv4 or IPv6 address. Returns country (name + ISO code), region (name + code), city, postal/ZIP, latitude/longitude (city-level precision, not GPS), timezone, ISP, organization, and AS number + name. Multi-gateway: the same lookup is available via four independent x402 providers at different prices and call conventions. GET https://2s.io/api/geo/ip?ip={ipv4_or_ipv6} (default). Other gateways: auor.io GET ?ip=, x402node GET ?ip=, padelmaps POST JSON {ip}. Output: Default (2s.io) is double-nested: data.items[0].{ip,country.{code,name},region.{code,name},city,postalCode,coords.{lat,lon},timezone,network.{isp,org,asn}} + data.source + meta.cost.usd. NOTE: padelmaps & x402node return a FLAT object instead.

target.description: IP address (v4 or v6) or domain name to look up (aliases accepted: ip, address, host, hostname, query — query param or JSON body)

usage.outputShape: target, ip, ip_version, hostname, asn, asn_number, organization, network, country, region, city, is_hosting, is_cloud, is_vpn, classification, score, grade, findings[].{rule,deduction,detail}

network field may come back null even when populated in the spec example

usage.outputShape: ip, reversed_ip, listed_count, total_checked, threat_level, score, grade, findings[], blacklists[].{name,listed,description}

IPv4 ONLY (input schema is ipv4-only, unlike the asn-lookup which accepts domains/IPv6)

name: DNS Lookup
description: DNS record lookup / DNS-over-HTTPS resolution for a domain (A, AAAA, MX, TXT, etc.). Pay-per-call x402 (multiple providers).

type.description: DNS record type: A, AAAA, MX, TXT, CNAME, NS, SOA, SRV (default: A)

usage.outputShape: body.records.<TYPE>[] (each {name,ttl,data}); convenience arrays at body.flat.{a,aaaa,mx,ns,txt,cname,caa}; body.domain, body.types_queried[], body.total_records, body.source
quirks: Service ignores any 'type' param and always queries all record types (A, AAAA, MX, TXT, NS, CAA) at once — read the type you want from body.records or body.flat.
No txHash returned by payment layer (confirmed=false), but call settled and returned 200.
usage.guide: POST to https://x402.agentutility.ai/dns-lookup with a JSON body containing {"domain":"<domain>"} and pay the $0.02 USDC x402 charge (Base, eip155:8453). The response is synchronous JSON. Read records by type at body.records (e.g. body.records.A[].data for IPv4) or use the flattened lists at body.flat (body.flat.a, body.flat.mx, body.flat.ns, etc.). It always returns all record types regardless of any 'type' field you send.

name: NetIntel IP Report
description: One call returns a complete five-part IP profile — geolocation, ASN/network ownership, multi-DNSBL blacklist status, threat reputation, and an aggregate block/allow risk verdict — run concurrently with graceful partial-failure handling.

ip.description: IPv4 or IPv6 address to profile (query param). Private/reserved ranges are rejected; the blacklist section is IPv4-only and reports error:"ipv4_only" for IPv6 input.

sections.description: geo, network, blacklist, reputation, risk — each with an `available` flag plus its own fields

usage.callShape: GET https://netintel.dev/ip-report/full?ip=<ipv4-or-ipv6> (x402, USDC on Base or Solana; the target IP is passed as the `ip` query param, no JSON body)
usage.outputShape: body.ip, body.generated_at, body.sections{geo,network,blacklist,reputation,risk} (each with .available + its fields, e.g. geo.country/city/timezone/isp, network.asn/organization/classification, blacklist.listed_count/lists_checked/listed_on[], reputation.abuse_confidence/otx_pulses, risk.risk_score/recommendation), body.sections_ok, body.sections_failed, body.overall_recommendation, body.score (0-100), body.grade (A-F), body.findings[]{rule,deduction,detail}
quirks: ip is a QUERY PARAM on a GET request (no JSON body): ?ip=8.8.8.8
Private/reserved IP ranges are rejected (SSRF-safe)
Blacklist section is IPv4-only — reports error:"ipv4_only" for IPv6 input; other sections still resolve for IPv6
Partial-failure tolerant: sections that fail come back with available:false; sections_ok/sections_failed report the split, and partials never read as safe
Failed calls (4xx/5xx, upstream failure, input rejection) are never charged (agent fair-trade)
usage.guide: Call GET https://netintel.dev/ip-report/full with a single query param `ip` set to an IPv4 or IPv6 address, e.g. ?ip=8.8.8.8. Pay via x402 (USDC on Base eip155:8453 or Solana), ~$0.20/call. The JSON response is returned synchronously (no polling): read body.overall_recommendation and body.risk.recommendation for the block/allow decision, body.score (0-100) + body.grade (A-F) for the aggregate verdict, and body.sections.{geo,network,blacklist,reputation,risk} for the five-part breakdown. Check each section's .available flag since sections degrade gracefully on partial failure.

name: NetIntel Subnet Calculator

usage.callShape: GET https://netintel.dev/subnet/calc?cidr=<cidr> (x402, USDC on Base eip155:8453 OR Solana; no JSON body; cidr is a query param)
usage.outputShape: cidr, ip_version, network, broadcast, netmask, wildcard, binary_mask, hex_mask, prefix_length, total_hosts, usable_hosts, first_usable, last_usable, is_private, supernet, subnets[].{prefix,count}, rfc_classification. Multi-CIDR (comma-separated) input returns {subnets, overlaps} instead.

Comma-separate multiple CIDRs (e.g. 10.0.0.0/16,10.0.1.0/24) to get overlap/containment analysis — the response shape switches to {subnets, overlaps} with each pair classified subnet/supernet/partial overlap/disjoint

name: 24kLabs IP / CIDR Subnet Calculator
description: CIDR/subnet math for IPv4 and IPv6: network, broadcast, netmask, wildcard, prefix length, usable host range and count, mask<->prefix conversion, plus an optional address-membership (contains) check.

cidr.description: The IPv4 or IPv6 network in CIDR notation, e.g. 192.168.1.0/24

contains.description: Optional IP address to test for membership within the CIDR block
Whether the optional 'contains' IP falls within the block (present only when 'contains' was supplied)

num_addresses is the total block size; usable_hosts excludes network + broadcast (254 for a /24).
Namespace alias /api/v1/ip-cidr-calc is the same op on the same host (deferred — index and pay only /api/ip-cidr-calc).
needs: A CIDR block string (e.g. 192.168.1.0/24); optionally an IP to test for membership.

The full subnet calculation — network, broadcast, netmask, wildcard, prefix, usable host range and count, and the optional membership boolean — comes back inline in the 200 response under result (synchronous, no polling).

The 402 body advertises a loyalty discount (X-Wallet header / ?wallet= drops the price to $0.0005 if the wallet spent >$0.001 in the last 24h) and an unrelated agent-memory upsell; neither affects the base call.
DST is reflected live: the documented example shows EST/-05:00 but a July call returns EDT/-04:00 for the same New York coordinates.
usage.guide: Get the timezone for a GPS coordinate. GET https://api.webbersites.com/api/timezone?lat={lat}&lng={lng} with lat (-90..90) and lng (-180..180) as query params. Returns a flat JSON object with the IANA timezone, utc_offset, utc_offset_minutes, abbreviation, dst_in_effect, and local_time. Pure x402 on Base USDC ($0.001/call), no auth. Pairs with an IP-geolocation lookup for scheduling/analytics agents.
